meta.title: CZ-8A Y13 · SatNet 50°
meta.subtitle: SatNet LEO group 30 · i 50.0° · 1049 km · long coast
about: Fitted to the NOTAM drop zones, four ground sightings and Y12's inserted orbit; not telemetry.
meta.tle_note: Model TLEs at the T0 above, retimed with it. Catalog numbers and designator are placeholders.
notes: Post-launch model, not telemetry and not an official ephemeris. CZ-8A Y13 (SatNet LEO group 30, nine satellites) lifted off from Hainan commercial pad LC1 at 19:59 Beijing time on 20 November 2026 (Xinhua). The model T0 is 11:59:59 UTC; the seconds are not published.

Lower stages: published sequence (boosters off T+171.9 s, stage 1 separation T+198.5 s, S2 ignition T+200.8 s, fairing T+209.4 s), fitted to the centroids of RPHI NOTAMs B6120/26 (boosters) and B6122/26 (core and fairing) and to four ground sightings from N 18°26′14″ E 110°04′28″ near Lingshui. The sightings fit to 0.77° at worst; the timed stage-1 separation is seen at 94.6/28.9° and modelled at 94.5/28.2°.

Open point: the sightings and zones fit together only if the core runs at 77.5 % thrust from T+10 s to booster separation. Lift-off is then 341.3 t against the published 371 t. The throttle stands in for whatever lowers the lower-stage energy; it is not claimed as fact.
S2 load 30.2 t (assumed). Burn 1 lasts 627 s to a 679 × 1061 km transfer orbit, followed by a 40.6 min long coast and a 5.3 s apogee burn on the inserted orbit; 1.01 t is left.

The inserted orbit is CZ-8A Y12's (2026-243) first element set moved in plane to Y13. The model reaches it with zero phase shift; its mean altitude is 1049.5 km at i 50.003°. Y12 flew the same profile. From the 1050 km parking orbit, J2 drift takes the group into the plane of 2025-295.

The page's perigee and apogee (1045.6 × 1057.7 km) are osculating after burn 2; the TLEs are SGP4 mean elements fitted to the model orbit. Catalog numbers 99913/99914 and the designator 26999 are placeholders. Deployment +120 s and disposal +300 s after burn 2 are assumptions.

Sunlight: geometric WGS84 occultation of the Sun's centre with DE440s, 30 s cadence. The powered ascent is in Earth's shadow; the vehicle first meets sunlight during the coast at T+30.0 min over New Zealand, and the apogee burn is in daylight. Shifting T0 on this page keeps the Earth-fixed path and moves only the Sun.
Pad 19.5970°N 110.9307°E (GCAT site record; GCAT's LC1 launch-point row lies 3.1 km south, at sea). Data: GCAT (J. McDowell, planet4589.org), Space-Track.org.

zones.label: 2 liquid boosters
zones.desc: RPHI NOTAM, fall area of unburned debris. The model puts the two K2 boosters here (separation T+171.9 s, fitted to the centroid).

zones.label: Core stage + fairing
zones.desc: RPHI NOTAM. The core (separation T+198.5 s) is fitted to the centroid; the fairing halves (T+209.4 s, ballistic coefficient 30) land here at T+1299 s without being fitted.
